findings.title: The hint also appears when the user is setting or bumping a version, where it doesn't make sense.
findings.body:
`find_target` is used for every `uv version` mode, not just reading the version. So `uv version 1.2.3`, `uv version --bump patch` or `uv version --package foo` with no `pyproject.toml` would also print "If you meant to view uv's version, use `uv self version` instead". In those cases the user was clearly trying to change a project, so the hint is misleading.

**Fix:** only add the hint when no value, `--bump` or `--package` was given.

held.title: The hint is baked into the error text, so the error loses its `WorkspaceError` type and the hint shows up wherever the message is reused.
held.body:
Before this change, `?` wrapped the `WorkspaceError` in anyhow and kept its type. Now a `MissingPyprojectToml` becomes a plain string error with the hint inside it. Two things can go wrong:

1. Any caller of `find_target` that runs `downcast_ref::<WorkspaceError>()` will stop matching.
2. Any caller that puts `{err}` into another message will carry the hint into that message. For example, a non-strict fallback warning like `Failed to read project metadata ({err}). Running uv self version…` would get a `\n\nhint: …` line in the middle of the warning.

The test name `version_get_fallback_missing_strict_preview` suggests such a fallback path exists, but I couldn't see the caller to confirm it.

**Fix:** keep the typed error and add the hint where the error is finally reported. If you do wrap it here, keep the source error with `.context()` or a typed wrapper rather than `anyhow!("{}", err)`, and don't duplicate the identical closure in both branches.
